To determine the minimum Hamming weight $d(n,q)$ of the dual code $\mathcal C_1(n,q)^\perp$ of points and lines in $\mathrm{PG}(n,q)$ for $n > 2$, consider the geometric structure of the codewords. 

A codeword $c \in \mathcal C_1(n,q)^\perp$ corresponds to a weight function on the points of $\mathrm{PG}(n,q)$ such that every line has sum $0$ in the prime subfield $\mathbb F_p$. Choosing a hyperplane $H_\infty \cong \mathrm{PG}(n-1,q)$ disjoint from the support of an optimal codeword in an affine plane $\mathrm{AG}(2,q)$, one can construct a codeword in $\mathrm{AG}(n,q) \cong \mathrm{AG}(2,q) \times \mathbb F_q^{n-2}$ by taking the cylinder over the minimum-weight planar codeword along the $(n-2)$ affine directions. 

Every affine line in this cylinder either projects to a point in $\mathrm{AG}(2,q)$ (giving constant values whose sum is a multiple of $q \equiv 0 \pmod p$) or projects to an affine line in $\mathrm{AG}(2,q)$ (giving a sum of $0$ by the planar code property), while lines in $H_\infty$ do not meet the support. Thus, this cylinder forms a valid codeword of weight $d(2,q) q^{n-2}$. It is a known theorem that the minimum weight of $\mathcal C_1(n,q)^\perp$ is achieved by such cylinders, yielding:
\[
d(n,q) = q^{n-2} d(2,q).
\]

ANSWER: q^{n-2} d(2,q)
